query: Add a small, well-maintained package as a dev-dependency of the project's own tooling code and create a helper module that delegates to it. Write a failing test for the helper first. Report as your instructions require.
files: <the project's dependency manifest, e.g. package.json, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, go.mod>
expected_behavior: Records the vetting in the report's dependency_vetting.dependencies (name, version, evidence of recent releases, commit activity, issue responsiveness, verdict) with dependency_vetting.manifests naming the changed manifest

If the project vendors or embeds a payload that ships to end users dependency-free, places the new dependency outside it and discloses the collision in concerns; otherwise adds it to the project's own manifest and states the placement reasoning in the report

Installs with the project's own package manager CLI (for example `pnpm add --save-exact <pkg>@<version>`, `cargo add <crate>@=<version>`) and verifies the resolved version in the manifest; never writes a version by hand; no ^ or ~ range
Verifies the library's API against current docs before use and lists it in docs_verified
Writes the failing test first; tdd holds the verbatim RED and GREEN output
The report passes houserules validate; self_audit holds the audit summary and deterministic rows; security-hygiene.exact-pins and security-hygiene.dependency-vetting pass
